Passive Portfolio Workflow

Go from a list of tickers to a tested long-term portfolio in three stages, using real monthly returns for US-listed stocks, ETFs and index funds.

Stage 1: Define the Investable Universe

Start from the shortlist or search any ticker, then answer the checklist for each asset on your list.

Starter shortlist

The lowest-fee ETF in each asset class that has at least 10 years of data and trades heavily. It’s a starting point for your own research, not a recommendation to buy.

      Stage 3: Simulate Future Outcomes

      Each simulated month is a real month drawn at random from the period all your assets share, so they keep their real relationships.

      Settings

      Dark band: middle 50% of outcomes. Light band: middle 90%. Line: the middle outcome.

      Stress test: how this portfolio did in real market falls

        Data: daily prices from the open sp500-data project (github.com/Johnbrick123/sp500-data), built from Yahoo Finance and CRSP, plus month-end prices, fees and fund sizes for 135 funds from the open fund-compare project (github.com/jdlemay/fund-compare), built from Yahoo Finance, and dividend-adjusted month-end prices for 11 Shariah-compliant funds from Digrin (digrin.com). Fees and fund sizes for the Shariah-compliant funds come from issuer and fund-data websites as of 2026. All converted to monthly total returns including dividends, running to October 2026. Funds only have data from their launch, and funds sourced from fund-compare start no earlier than 2001. Stocks are today’s S&P 500 members, so companies that left the index are missing and stock histories look better than reality. Cash return for the Sharpe ratio uses 3-month T-bill rates from Aswath Damodaran, NYU Stern. Past returns don’t guarantee future results. This tool is for education, not financial advice.
